quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging.
Multiple turns ahead.
The lane is shifting.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare you for road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let other vehicles merge safely.

questions.question: What do flashing amber lights on a school bus mean?

options.text: The bus has finished loading or unloading children.
The bus is about to stop. Be ready to stop.
The bus is broken down. You can pass slowly.
The bus is loading or unloading. You can go slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus is about to stop. Be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Flashing amber lights warn you that the bus will stop to load or unload children. Get ready to stop. When red lights flash, stop your car and wait until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use a different route.
Drive the same as you do on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other cars.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the space between your car and the car ahead. Your car will take longer to stop on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass carefully.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When must you stop for a pedestrian crossing?

options.text: Only in marked crosswalks.
In marked or unmarked crosswalks.
Only if the pedestrian is directly in front of you.
Only if there is a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: In marked or unmarked crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop for pedestrians at any marked or unmarked crosswalk. Let them cross safely, then proceed.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways and proceed with caution.

questions.question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect a driver?

options.text: It does not cause driving errors.
It makes them drive too slowly.
It makes them better drivers because they are not hungry.
It makes it hard to control the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes it hard to control the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. You will have trouble keeping your car in its lane and controlling it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass carefully.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is coming. The road splits into two one-way lanes separated by a divider. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop completely. You must stop before entering the intersection. Driving through a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You may turn right on a red light if a sign does not forbid it.

questions.question: How do drowsy drivers affect road safety?

options.text: They should drink strong coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window or turning up the radio.
Only older drivers get drowsy.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers perform so poorly they may seem drunk. Opening a window, playing loud music, or drinking coffee will not keep a drowsy driver alert enough to avoid hazards.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be held safely by a strong adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Special child seats are available for small children who cannot use regular safety belts. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper seat for children.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through with caution.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move as far to the right side of the road as possible before turning right. Do not cut across lanes of traffic.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Never move the injured person.
Avoid moving them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid moving them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Not necessary.
Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: While backing up, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look out the rear window while backing. Do not depend only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
You see a police car.
Entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: When roads are wet, icy, or slippery, or when you cannot see well, drive below the speed limit. Even if you are going the posted speed, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: Always try to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter the situation. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and let them cross safely, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hit the brakes hard.
Grip the wheel firmly and slow down gradually to a stop.
Drive normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the wheel firmly and slow down gradually to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Hold the wheel tight and steer to stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the accelerator. Once you are going very slowly, lightly apply the brakes and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to your emergency.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Road hazard warning.
Interstate route sign.
School crossing sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow (or orange in work areas) and warn you about hazards ahead or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that workers may be on or very close to the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents other vehicles from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to surprises.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to respond to mistakes or problems. This extra time can prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
Motorcycle brake lights come on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Your entire vehicle must be in the left lane before and during passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
A steep hill is coming.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is coming.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on yellow (or orange in work areas). This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Be ready to adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes caused by alcohol?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks and offer to be the driver.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead not to drive if you drink. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is hard to make safe choices after drinking starts.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into the lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than traffic flow can be unsafe. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you, you must pull over and let cars pass. Only drive well under the speed limit if road conditions require it.

questions.question: To avoid fatigue on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours on long trips to take a short break. If you feel drowsy, pull over and park safely to nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you must always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before turning across train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: Oregon's Implied Consent Law means that by driving in the state, you agree to:

options.text: Keep liability insurance while you drive.
Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
Post bail or appear in court if arrested for a traffic violation.
Keep your vehicle in safe working condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
questions.explanation: Under Oregon's Implied Consent Law, by driving in the state you agree to take a breath, blood, or urine test if a police officer asks you after arresting you for driving under the influence.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against a red light or are being careless.
